_comment: First relative risk computed from a cohort table: two incidences, then their ratio. Illustrative numbers.

stem.en: Illustrative cohort. Of 1,200 men exposed to a solvent, 60 develop the disease over ten years of follow-up; of 800 unexposed men, 16 develop it over the same ten years. Compute the relative risk, to 2 decimal places.

explanation.en: The incidence among the exposed is 60/1,200 = 0.05, or 50 per 1,000 over ten years; among the unexposed it is 16/800 = 0.02, or 20 per 1,000. The relative risk is the ratio of the two incidences, 0.05/0.02 = 2.50, so exposed men had 2.50 times the risk of unexposed men over the same period.

hints.en: Divide the cases by their own cohort's total first; only then divide the exposed incidence by the unexposed incidence.
